## Item 8: the Ritual admin edits a row that holds an unregistered path

- Head: d9cc6da10ccd35cb27d08b295f4130eabca5494b
- Did: created a Ritual row directly in the database (not through the admin) with `service_function_path` `world.old.hearth_rite`, a path that is not in the registry. As a staff superuser, opened its admin change page and read the service select back. Posted the change form with only the description changed, then posted it with the path changed to a different unregistered path, `world.other.cold_rite`. After each post, read the saved row from the database.
- Expected: the select lists the thread retune path and the re-swearing path, and shows the stored unregistered path marked as not registered so the row stays editable. A save that leaves the path alone succeeds and keeps the path. A save that moves the path to another unregistered one is refused and the row is unchanged.
- Saw:
  - The select options include `world.magic.services.thread_resonance.change_thread_resonance` ("Magic: retune a thread") and `world.covenants.focus_picks.reswear_vow_pick` ("Covenants: Rite of Re-swearing"). The stored path is the selected option, labelled "world.old.hearth_rite (not registered)".
  - Changing only the description: HTTP 302 to `/admin/arxii/ritual/`. The row afterwards has description "The hearth is lit and banked." (was "The hearth is lit.") and `service_function_path` still `world.old.hearth_rite`.
  - Changing the path to `world.other.cold_rite`: HTTP 200 (the form again), with the error "Select a valid choice. world.other.cold_rite is not one of the available choices." The row afterwards is unchanged, path still `world.old.hearth_rite`. The refusal text is Django's own choice-field message; the form's own wording "That is not a service a ritual may run." was not reached because the select refuses first.
  - Also recorded, for the "same fields as before" check: the change and add forms list the same 19 fields in the same order as a plain ModelForm over `fields = "__all__"` minus the two read-only columns (`execution_kind`, `flow`), with nothing on only one side.
- Files: payloads/40-admin-edit-unregistered-path-row.json, payloads/41-admin-form-fields-same-as-before.json, payloads/01-admin-creates-the-rite.json (the add flow, re-recorded at this head: 24 services listed, `os.system` refused, a row created through the select with its component).

## Item 9: the real Required content endpoint as staff

- Head: d9cc6da10ccd35cb27d08b295f4130eabca5494b
- Did: as a staff superuser, requested `/admin/_ops/required-content/` and read the rows that name the Rite of Re-swearing out of the page's tables. Case one: two re-swearing rites, both made through the Ritual admin add form choosing the re-swearing service ("Rite of Re-swearing" and "Second Re-swearing"). Case two: one rite, made through the admin add form with a component row set to a target-resonance offering; then, to show the consequence the row names, read the options endpoint, performed the rite over the web and typed `vow reswear Quick Recovery=Feint and Vanish` on telnet.
- Expected: with two rites the page lists the second by name; with a target-resonance offering it lists the rite as unpayable; neither case leaves the "missing rite" Required row.
- Saw:
  - Two rites: the Tuning table has the row "Only one Rite of Re-swearing", Missing column "Second Re-swearing 2 rituals change a chosen vow pick; the sheet and vow reswear perform only Rite of Re-swearing. Remove or repoint: Second Re-swearing." Before any rite the Required table had the row "Rite of Re-swearing" with "no SERVICE ritual has the service path world.covenants.focus_picks.reswear_vow_pick"; with the rites made that row is gone.
  - Target-resonance offering: the Tuning table has the row "Rite of Re-swearing payable", Missing column "Rite of Re-swearing Rite of Re-swearing asks for a target-resonance offering; the rite names no resonance, so it can never be paid." The options endpoint answers 200 with components ["an offering"] and component_ids []. The web perform answers 400 "Ritual 'Rite of Re-swearing' needs a target resonance." and telnet prints the same sentence. Afterwards action points are still 10 and Quick Recovery is still the chosen pick.
- Files: payloads/50-required-content-two-reswearing-rites.json, payloads/51-required-content-unpayable-component.json

## Item 10: the membership lock in choose_vow_focus_pick and reswear_vow_pick

- Head: d9cc6da10ccd35cb27d08b295f4130eabca5494b for the branch; 731a2ae4fd5192d16b1c49cffee59e59767f705f (origin/main) for the old behaviour
- Did: wrapped a real call in `CaptureQueriesContext` and saved every SQL statement in order. Branch, choose: `dispatch_player_action` for `choose_vow_focus_pick` (the web dispatch seam). Branch, re-swear: `POST /api/magic/rituals/perform/` through the real view, `PerformRitualAction` and `reswear_vow_pick`. Main, choose: the same dispatch call at origin/main. In each run the membership instance had been created in the same process, so the idmapper holds it, as in the single server process.
- Expected: a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the character's covenant membership row before the already-chosen check, the budget check and the write.
- Saw:
  - Branch, choose (33 statements): statement 14 is `SELECT "arxii_charactercovenantrole"."id" AS "pk" FROM "arxii_charactercovenantrole" WHERE ("arxii_charactercovenantrole"."id" = 11 AND "arxii_charactercovenantrole"."left_at" IS NULL) FOR UPDATE`, then the already-chosen check (15), then the INSERT of the pick (27).
  - Branch, re-swear (78 statements): the membership lock is statement 48, the same pk-only query with `FOR UPDATE`. Statements 19 and 41 are the two unlocked check passes (the action's precheck and the service's first check), 53 is the re-check under the lock, then the DELETE of the given-up pick (59), the INSERT of the new one (63), `FOR UPDATE` on the action point pool row (66) and its UPDATE to 7 (68).
  - Old behaviour at origin/main, choose (33 statements): a FOR UPDATE was not missing. Statement 14 is `SELECT <every membership column> FROM "arxii_charactercovenantrole" WHERE "arxii_charactercovenantrole"."id" = 15 LIMIT 21 FOR UPDATE`, from `select_for_update().get(pk=...)`, followed by the same already-chosen check (15) and INSERT (27). So the lock existed at main even with the row already in the idmapper cache; the branch's change from `.get()` to a pk-only filter that also requires `left_at IS NULL` locks the same row, and is not a fix for a missing lock.
  - A concurrent double-spend was not reproduced and not attempted. Two real connections need a `TransactionTestCase`, which flushes the test database when it ends, and no database is flushed here. What is shown is the SQL a single real call emits, and that at main and on the branch the lock statement comes before the check and the write.
- Notes on the main run: the shared test schema was built from the branch and has one extra NOT NULL column (`respec_ap_cost` on `arxii_vowfocuspickconfig`) that main's code does not know, so that run's test set a column default inside its own transaction, which rolled back with the test (read back afterwards: no default on the column).
- Files: payloads/60-choose-vow-focus-pick-sql-head.json, payloads/61-reswear-vow-pick-sql-head.json, payloads/62-choose-vow-focus-pick-sql-main.json
